excerpt: Masterise Accountability Index (MAI) Black Points System Manual & Guidelines Version 1.2 – April 2025 1: PURPOSE & SCOPE In our current operations, performance tracking of project stakeholders often depends on informal impressions or verbal feedback. This creates risk in repeated engagement of underperforming contractors, weak oversight, and inconsistent project outcomes. The Masterise Accountability Index (MAI) is introduced as a structured Black Points System that builds a data-based performance history for every key party on site. With this system, we aim to:  Eliminate subjectivity in evaluating stakeholders  Prevent rework and recurring mistakes  Protect project timelines and brand reputation  Strengthen contractor accountability and selection processes MAI assigns transparent scores for quality, safety, and compliance violations, categorized by severity. It tracks:  Main Contractors  PMCM (Project Management/Consultant Managers)  Nominated Subcontractors (NSCs)  Consultants  Individuals (site-level staff not employed by the Developer) It provides long-term visibility and control across Masterise projects, ensuring risk is managed proactively and repeat violations are discouraged. 2: STAKEHOLDER RESPONSIBILITIES The MAI system applies to key external project stakeholders involved in execution, supervision, and design. Internal Masterise staff are not scored but support the system's enforcement. Stakeholder Responsibilities Main Contractor Supervise NSCs, ensure ITP compliance, escalate NCRs/SVRs, manage workmanship PMCM Enforce QAQC/HSE processes, coordinate reviews, respond to risks timely NSC (Nominated Subcontractor) Execute works as per approved drawings and ITPs, ensure HSE compliance Consultant Submit accurate, coordinated designs; update drawings and respond promptly Individuals (External site-level staff) QAQC, HSE, engineers or supervisors working on site under contractor/consultant roles are scored based on honesty, presence, and compliance. OBJECTIVE: Objective of this procedure is to provide minimum requirements for lockout and tag out of energy- isolating devices to protect any Person from hazardous energy including electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, or any other energy. 2. SCOPE: 2.1. This procedure applies to all operating and project sites of ███ and all its Contractors. 3. EXPECTED RESULTS: 3.1. Manage jobs being done involving energy sources safely. 3.2. Control of incidents in Jobs involving sources of energy. 3.3. Compliance to Regulatory requirements related to safety from energy sources. 4. ACCOUNTABILITY & RESPONSIBILITY: 4.1. ACCOUNTABILITY: Concerned Divisional Heads / Asset Custodians. 4.2. RESPONSIBILITY: 4.2.1. Permit Acceptor shall be responsible to ensure that only trained and authorized people are deployed for the jobs. 4.2.2. Person In-Charge/Shift In-Charge (Permit Issuer) shall be responsible for but not limited to isolation / draining / blinding / venting of process equipment before releasing it for maintenance / inspection in their respective plants/areas. 4.2.3. Maintenance Supervisors shall be responsible for maintenance activities as per the process requirements and must use appropriate Personal protective equipment while carrying out maintenance activities. 4.2.4. Person In-Charge/Shift In-Charge and all the concerned permit holders of the job shall be responsible for lockout and tag out Note: Refer Annexure – 1 for detailed Responsibility Matrix. 5. GLOSSARY/ DEFINITIONS: Authorized person: A qualified Person trained and authorized in the lockout/tag out procedure to make and verify isolations. Control device: A device used to execute a system change by manual, remote, automatic, or partially automatic means (e.g., push buttons, emergency buttons or stops, selector switches, and other control-circuit type devices). Danger Tag: A tag that is placed with intention of warning to the persons that device is under isolation and must not be operated/switched on.

Also referred as “Proprietor / Owner” in the ███ LOTO Standard. Qualified Person: A Person trained and authorized to work with the equipment and who understands the hazards involved. Risk Assessment: A systematic and structured process whereby hazards present in a workplace, or arising from workplace activity, are identified, risks assessed / evaluated, and decisions prioritized in order to reduce risks to acceptable levels. Risk: The likelihood (probability) which can lead to potential negative consequences. Severity: The level of consequence / harm of an event that could occur due to exposure to the hazard present Shall: Mandatory requirement Should: Optional requirement Stored energy: Hazardous energy that can continue to exist after equipment is isolated (e.g., the hazardous energy contained in springs, flywheels, pressurized fluids or gases, pneumatically controlled devices, capacitors, or gravity). Tagging: Placing a specific tag on a lock or point of isolation to identify who placed the lock and when it was placed. Tag out: Placement of danger tag Task / Activity: A sequence of steps taken to conduct a job. A task is a sub element of a Job. Team Leader: A qualified and authorized Person who shall undertake overall responsibility for a lockout/tag out to place and keep all hazardous energy sources under lockout/tag out and to account for all Persons working with him on the job or task. The top third section of the SI form shall be completed by describing the work which needs to be changed / altered. The PMC shall obtain the Employer project manager’s signature on the form for any site instruction that has cost and / or time implication under the Contract. The Contractor shall be responsible for responding to the SI in a timely manner by identifying the measures which shall be taken and notify the PM/CS when the action is completed. The Contractor shall discuss with the PM/CS his proposal prior to executing the works. If the Contractor fails to comply with the SIR and complete the works satisfactorily within the specified time, the PM/CS shall issue a Non-Conformance Report (NCR) due to such default and payment for the affected work or material withheld. DISTRIBUTION Site Instructions shall be distributed as follows: Original and a copy to Contractor. The Contractor signs and dates both documents and returns the copy to the PM/CS as acknowledgement of receipt of the SI form. excerpt: NON-CONFORMANCE REPORT (NCR) BÁO CÁO KHÔNG PHÙ HỢP GUIDANCE ON FORM USE An NCR can be initiated by any project team member upon observation. The observation is to be communicated to the PM/CS who will assess the observation and determine if an NCR is warranted, The PM/CS will complete part 1 of the NCR clearly detailing: - details of the observation - Variation from the specification / drawings - Identify if the NCR is related to a process or material/ product. (Analytics) The NCR will be issued to the Contractor responsible. The Contractor will review the NCR and issue a (1st) response within 3 days by completing Part 2 of the form. The response will include as a mimimun: - Details of proposed remedial action. - Calculations if required. - Brief / detailed Method statement for the remedial works. - details of specific materials to be used. DO not use MAR for this step. - Analytics - Declare: Replace, Repair, Use as is. - Analytics - 5 M root cause. - An NCR should be closed within 28days. If this is no achieveable the contractor should set a target date. The PM/CS will review that proposed rectifcation works. The PMCS may request a review by Design if considered appropriate. The PM/CS will return his review code to the Contractor using art 3 of the form. - Review Code A: Contractor can proceed with the recrification works. - Review Code B: The proposed rectification work are acceptable in principle but additonal information required. - Revoew Code C: Not approved. Contractor to look at alternative methods. The contractor will continue to submit/resubmit the proposed rectification works thought 2nd, 3rd, 4th .. response until Review Status A is received, Upon Receipt of Status A, the Contractor will execute the rectification works. Once the recification works are completed, the contractor will call for a works inspection (WIR) to have the works accepted. Once the WIR is accepted by the PMCS, The NCR will be closed and signed off by: - Contractor - QAQC - MRH Rep. (PD/PM) The NCR Register will be updated accordling. NOTE: Technical Submittal Form and Material Approval Request forms are not requried for submitting attachme
